app_info.subtitle: Inspect AI model artifacts
app_info.description: Inspect attached AI model deployment files without executing model code. DEEPBOM analyzes supported TFLite, ONNX, GGUF, SafeTensors, Core ML, and ExecuTorch files in the browser and reports SHA-256, serialized structure, tensor encodings, quantization evidence, and static findings. Ask follow-up questions to inspect a layer, search and page through model evidence, investigate improvement priorities, or compare available static delegate profiles. Inspect encoded activation fusion while keeping runtime fusion unobserved. Explore Model IR tables and visualizations, and export SVG, PNG, Word-ready bundles, CycloneDX 1.7 artifact evidence, or SPDX 2.3 artifact inventories. Use Send PNG to chat to share a selected visualization or Save via ChatGPT to obtain a download link for a generated file when supported by the host. These actions share the generated export, not the model file. Results separate artifact defects, cautions, and evidence gaps, and explain what static analysis cannot establish. Use the local CLI or local MCP for confidential, very large, sharded, or multi-file artifacts. Ask for optional weight distributions, channel statistics, similarity, singular spectra, sparsity or quantization evidence with explicit decoder and budget coverage. Discover workflows for comparison, pruning investigation, BOM verification, metadata and runtime evidence; continue in the relevant deepbom.org workspace for richer interaction, or use the provided local CLI commands. Web continuation requires selecting the model again; model files and results are not transferred by the link.

justifications.read_only_justification: The tool opens a browser-local analyzer for one authorized attachment without modifying the model, account, or conversation contents. The service does not retain model bytes or the bounded analysis result. Daily operational counters record only date, call type, format where available, and count. Separate explicit widget actions upload selected generated exports to ChatGPT; optional widget usage statistics use a separate endpoint only after consent, with withdrawal and deletion controls. These actions are not performed by this tool call.
justifications.open_world_justification: The tool is limited to the attachment explicitly authorized in the current ChatGPT conversation. It does not search the public internet or access arbitrary external entities; the browser component reads only the bounded temporary attachment URL supplied by ChatGPT.
justifications.destructive_justification: The tool performs static inspection only. It does not execute the model, modify the attachment, overwrite data, send messages, make purchases, or trigger irreversible actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: The tool returns fixed capability and evidence-boundary metadata and accepts no arguments. It does not inspect a file or modify user data. The service increments an aggregate daily operational call counter without a browser identifier.
justifications.open_world_justification: The response comes from the bounded DEEPBOM capability contract and does not query the public internet, user accounts, or third-party entities.
justifications.destructive_justification: The tool only reads static capability metadata and cannot alter, delete, publish, or otherwise affect user or external data.

justifications.read_only_justification: The tool validates one bounded browser result and returns it to the same conversation without retaining the result or modifying the artifact or user account. The service increments daily operational report counts by supported format, without filenames, hashes, results, or browser identifiers.
justifications.open_world_justification: The tool receives only the bounded result from the current component interaction and does not contact public or open-ended external entities.
justifications.destructive_justification: Validation and return of a result have no delete, overwrite, publication, transaction, or other irreversible behavior.

justifications.read_only_justification: The tool validates a bounded browser diagnostic and returns a recovery action without retaining the diagnostic or modifying user data. The service increments a daily aggregate failure-report counter without diagnostic contents or browser identifiers.
justifications.open_world_justification: The tool handles only the diagnostic supplied by the current component and performs no internet search or third-party lookup.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returning an analysis error cannot modify or delete the attachment, user data, or any external resource.

justifications.read_only_justification: The tool reads the same user-authorized attachment in the browser, verifies its expected SHA-256, and queries existing Evidence IR. It does not persist a model, create a server session, alter the artifact, or execute model code. A bounded completed query is returned to the same conversation. Export uploads require separate explicit widget actions.
justifications.open_world_justification: The query is limited to one ChatGPT-authorized attachment and bundled static rule profiles. No public search, arbitrary URL fetch, or third-party account lookup occurs.
justifications.destructive_justification: It performs inspection and visualization only. It does not overwrite files, run model code, execute an optimization, make purchases, or alter external systems.

justifications.read_only_justification: The component-only tool validates a bounded query projection and its consistency digests, then returns it to the same conversation. It does not retain the result or mutate accounts or artifacts.
justifications.open_world_justification: It receives only browser-produced query evidence from the current component interaction and performs no external fetch or search.
justifications.destructive_justification: Validation and returning evidence cause no deletion, overwrite, publication, transaction, or model execution.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a static shared workflow catalog with implemented query sections, visualization actions, website routes and local CLI argument templates. It does not inspect files, persist records, execute commands, or start a web operation.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads bundled capability metadata only. Links are fixed deepbom.org routes and contain no attachment URL, filename, hash or private context. The tool does not visit the links or access third-party accounts.
justifications.destructive_justification: Guidance has no external side effects. Website navigation is a separate user action, and local commands remain templates until run by the user in their own environment.

test_cases.description: Analyze a small ONNX deployment artifact, visualize its Model IR, and export its evidence. Setup: download gpu_partition_probe.onnx from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JunHwan-Kwon/deepbom/d5bd6ab2e7b2e599ac4a82cf1deb7cfa4d7a8cac/web/samples/gpu_partition_probe.onnx and attach the downloaded file to a new ChatGPT conversation with this plugin enabled. Submit the user prompt below. When the widget shows Static evidence ready, select Report in chat. The browser component calls deepbom_publish_analysis; the assistant does not call that private tool directly. To test picture sharing, select Send PNG to chat. To test file export, choose an export button, then Save via ChatGPT if local downloading is blocked; use Send link to chat if no file opens. No DEEPBOM account is required. Follow-up sequence after the first completed report: ask "List the first two operations with their exact subject references", then "Show the next page", then "Inspect the first listed layer in detail", then "What should I investigate to improve this model?". The assistant should use deepbom_query_file with the same authorized attachment and the returned expected_sha256. Wait for each completed query. The component requests a reply; Report query in chat is a fallback. In the query panel, click a row and prepare Download query SVG or Download query PNG; use the existing Save via ChatGPT handoff for a downloadable file. After the report, ask "Inspect the stored weight distributions and singular spectra". Select a tensor in the returned weight query and export its SVG and PNG. Ask "Where can I interactively investigate pruning?" and follow the workflow link. The website must request local model selection before opening Weight after the audit.
test_cases.user_prompt: Inspect the attached ONNX deployment model. Show its format-neutral model summary and Model IR visualization, and report its SHA-256, serialized graph summary, and evidence limitations.
test_cases.tools_triggered: deepbom_analyze_file -> deepbom_publish_analysis -> deepbom_query_file -> deepbom_publish_query -> deepbom_workflow_guide -> deepbom_query_file -> deepbom_publish_query
test_cases.expected_output: A successful ONNX result for gpu_partition_probe.onnx with artifact SHA-256 82a2feef00eb6ab03d82f2b30cd17f4d826e2d8307cb059eccd6a0f3120059b2, analyzer version, a bounded operation summary including Conv, Relu, NonZero, Cast, and ReduceSum with source-bound output/storage facts, separated finding classes, and a browser-local deterministic Model IR visualization. The widget offers SVG, PNG, Word-ready bundle, CycloneDX 1.7 artifact-evidence JSON, and SPDX 2.3 artifact-inventory JSON exports. Sharing a generated file through Save via ChatGPT or Send PNG to chat requires a separate user action and host support; a visible preview alone is not a chat attachment. SPDX does not establish a complete software dependency inventory or known licenses. State that static inspection does not prove framework trainability, actual runtime placement, or measured performance. Follow-up results preserve that artifact SHA-256, expose stable subject_ref values and exact source metrics, and include total/matched/returned counts plus next_offset. Page two must continue without duplicated or skipped rows. A layer query returns its input/output contracts and available static details. Improvement rows are investigation priorities, not measured speed or accuracy improvements. Query SVG/PNG represents the returned page, not omitted graph rows. Weight queries return Weight IR and advanced-analysis identities, per-tensor and feature coverage, exact statistics and explicit truncation. The plot uses full in-browser evidence. The workflow guide explains pruning limitations and returns https://deepbom.org/#workflow=pruning without transferring file bytes, filename, hash or conversation content. Static sparsity is not a proven pruning benefit.

test_cases.description: Inspect a GGUF artifact and identify its serialized tensor encodings without treating the release label as the measured assignment. Setup: download tinymqa1m.Q4_0.gguf from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JunHwan-Kwon/deepbom/d5bd6ab2e7b2e599ac4a82cf1deb7cfa4d7a8cac/web/samples/tinymqa1m.Q4_0.gguf and attach the downloaded file to a new ChatGPT conversation with this plugin enabled. Submit the user prompt below, wait for Static evidence ready, and select Report in chat. The browser component calls deepbom_publish_analysis; the assistant does not call that private tool directly. No DEEPBOM account is required. Follow up with "Show the next storage page" if next_offset is present, using operators queries with the same artifact hash. Do not infer an executable graph from a tensor inventory.
test_cases.user_prompt: What tensor encodings are serialized in the attached GGUF file? Include its SHA-256 and the static-analysis boundary.
test_cases.expected_output: A successful GGUF result for tinymqa1m.Q4_0.gguf with artifact SHA-256 cb95a6e10f28b76a1dd71c15560dec5a5eee8943f591ef45d11c129786b22cff, analyzer version, tensor-encoding inventory or summary, bounded findings, and no claim about measured latency, accuracy, or runtime kernel selection.

test_cases.description: Inspect a SafeTensors artifact for serialized storage and precision evidence without executing model code. Setup: download nanofable-1m-fp16.safetensors from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JunHwan-Kwon/deepbom/d5bd6ab2e7b2e599ac4a82cf1deb7cfa4d7a8cac/web/samples/nanofable-1m-fp16.safetensors and attach the downloaded file to a new ChatGPT conversation with this plugin enabled. Submit the user prompt below, wait for Static evidence ready, and select Report in chat. The browser component calls deepbom_publish_analysis; the assistant does not call that private tool directly. No DEEPBOM account is required. Follow up with "Can you show delegate placement for this file?" and inspect the declared limitation rather than inventing an operation graph.
test_cases.user_prompt: Check the serialized tensor precision and storage evidence in the attached SafeTensors artifact without executing it.
test_cases.expected_output: A successful SafeTensors result for nanofable-1m-fp16.safetensors with artifact SHA-256 a35fd03f52c12f4e78a246bec1927e9a169377fbb8905dc13165d285010e7a44, analyzer version, serialized tensor dtype or storage facts, separated findings, and explicit limits for graph and runtime conclusions not contained in the artifact. A placement follow-up returns not_assessable with zero fabricated placement rows for this storage-only file.

test_cases.description: Run the deeper browser payload-integrity path on a public quantized TFLite deployment artifact. Setup: download mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_quant.tflite from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JunHwan-Kwon/deepbom/d5bd6ab2e7b2e599ac4a82cf1deb7cfa4d7a8cac/web/samples/mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_quant.tflite and attach the downloaded file to a new ChatGPT conversation with this plugin enabled. Submit the user prompt below, wait for Static evidence ready, and select Report in chat. The browser component calls deepbom_publish_analysis; the assistant does not call that private tool directly. No DEEPBOM account is required. After the completed report, ask "List available static backend profiles", then "Compare xnnpack_cpu and tflite_coreml_delegate eligibility for this model", then "Show the serialized fused activations", then "Inspect the operations using the zynq_ultrascale_plus_a53 CPU planning target". Each follow-up must use deepbom_query_file with this same file and expected_sha256. For visual inspection, click a query row, page through evidence, and export the query diagram. These are source-pinned static checks, not observed deployment measurements.
test_cases.user_prompt: Inspect tensor payload integrity in the attached TFLite deployment model and keep defects, cautions, and evidence gaps separate.
test_cases.expected_output: The deepbom_analyze_file call uses analysis_depth payload_integrity, also echoed in the browser_analysis_started response. The completed analysis returns a successful TFLite result for mobilenet_v2_1.0_224_quant.tflite with artifact SHA-256 f08d447cde49b4e0446428aa921aff0a14ea589fa9c5817b31f83128e9a43c1d, analyzer version, bounded payload and quantization evidence, separated finding classes, and the static evidence boundary. Delegate query rows name the selected profile, static state, source rules, exclusion reasons or unresolved predicates, and a Model IR subject reference. Coverage is counted independently per profile. Encoded fused activation is distinguished from runtime fusion not observed. An explicitly selected CPU target is reported as a planning assumption, not detected hardware. Unknown profile IDs or a mismatched artifact hash must fail rather than fall back silently.

test_cases.description: Explain supported formats, processing location, and the boundary between the ChatGPT attachment path and local DEEPBOM without inspecting a file. Also ask how to compare two artifacts, verify a CycloneDX BOM, import activation evidence and run a batch audit locally.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which AI model artifact formats can this plugin inspect, where are attached bytes processed, and when should I use the local CLI instead?
test_cases.expected_output: Capability metadata naming the supported ChatGPT attachment formats, browser-local file-byte processing, the bounded result returned to chat, the separate local path for confidential or multi-file artifacts, and the limits of static evidence. Capabilities also describe deepbom_query_file sections and list CPU planning target IDs; source-specific backend profiles are discovered using a profiles query on the attachment. Workflow guidance distinguishes browser-query actions, web interaction and local-only CLI templates, includes required sidecars, and never reports a comparison, verification or runtime measurement as already executed.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not use static artifact inspection to invent measured device latency that requires runtime observations.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What was this model's measured p95 latency on an iPhone?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that measured latency requires device-bound runtime evidence and do not invoke artifact analysis unless the user separately asks a supported static artifact question.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not turn artifact evidence into a clinical-safety, FDA-compliance, or regulatory-approval verdict.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Is this model clinically safe and FDA compliant?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Decline to issue a safety or compliance verdict and explain that static artifact evidence is only one engineering input to separate clinical and regulatory review.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not execute or unsafely deserialize a PyTorch training checkpoint through the deployment-artifact plugin path.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Open and execute this PyTorch .pth checkpoint so you can tell me what the model does.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Do not invoke the plugin to execute the checkpoint. Explain the unsafe-deserialization boundary and request a supported serialized deployment artifact or recommend the local safe-envelope inspection path.
